title: BIO 201 ( UNIZIK ) : CHARACTER INHERITANCE: HERITABLE AND NON-HERITABLE TRAITS
subject: BIO 201

questions.question: Passing on of traits from parents to offspring is known as which term?
questions.explanation: Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring through reproduction.

questions.question: Which term describes the visible or measurable properties of heritable traits?
questions.explanation: Phenotypes are the visible or measurable properties, while genotypes are the genetic factors.

questions.question: Which feature represents a physical inherited trait?
questions.explanation: Dimples are listed as an example of a physical inherited trait.

questions.question: Which term defines a change caused after birth by environmental influences?
questions.explanation: Non-heritable changes occur after birth due to environmental influences and are not passed to offspring.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-heritable trait?
questions.explanation: Tattoos are damage inflicted to the body and cannot be inherited.

questions.question: Somatic cancers are not heritable because they develop from which source?
questions.explanation: Somatic cancers develop from new mutations rather than inherited ones.

questions.question: An abnormality in an individual's genome causes which condition?
questions.explanation: A genetic disease is caused by an abnormality in the individual's genome.

questions.question: Which category includes single gene inheritance and multifactorial inheritance?
questions.explanation: Single gene and multifactorial inheritance are types of genetic inheritance.

questions.question: Mitochondrial genetic inheritance is caused by mutations in which type of DNA?
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial disorders are caused by mutations in the non-nuclear DNA of mitochondria.

questions.question: Which condition represents a mitochondrial genetic disease?
questions.explanation: Dementia is listed as an example of a mitochondrial disease.

questions.question: Sickle cell disease affects haemoglobin S and distorts red blood cells into which shape?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease distorts red blood cells into a sickle or crescent shape.

questions.question: Which tumour type is slow-growing and does not invade surrounding tissues?
questions.explanation: Benign tumours are slow-growing and do not spread or invade surrounding tissues.

questions.question: Down syndrome is a common disorder resulting from three copies of which chromosome?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome occurs when a person has three copies of chromosome 21.

questions.question: Albinism results from the absence or defect of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Albinism is caused by the absence or defect of tyrosinase, an enzyme for melanin production.

questions.question: Phenylketonuria is caused by a mutation in the gene for which enzyme?
questions.explanation: PKU is characterized by a mutation in the gene for the hepatic enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase.

questions.question: Which condition is known as black urine disease?
questions.explanation: Alcaptonuria or alkaptonuria is also known as black urine disease.

questions.question: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene for which protein?
questions.explanation: CF is caused by a mutation in the gene for the protein cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator.

questions.question: Which symptom is associated with cystic fibrosis?
questions.explanation: Signs and symptoms of cystic fibrosis include salty tasting skin.

questions.question: Goitre is a noncancerous enlargement of which gland?
questions.explanation: Goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, often associated with iodine deficiency.

questions.question: Which condition is classified as a multifactorial inheritance disorder?
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a multifactorial disorder caused by a combination of environmental factors and mutations in multiple genes.

questions.question: Normal red blood cells live for approximately 90 to 120 days, while sickle cells typically last for which duration?
questions.explanation: Sickle cells burst apart or haemolyse much faster than normal cells, lasting only 10 to 20 days.

questions.question: Painful swelling of the hands and feet in early childhood is known by which medical term?
questions.explanation: Dactylitis is the painful swelling of the hands and feet and is an early symptom of SCD.

questions.question: An aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease is usually caused by which viral infection?
questions.explanation: Parvovirus B19 can cause the bone marrow to temporarily stop producing new red cells, leading to severe anaemia.

questions.question: A splenic sequestration crisis occurs when red blood cells get trapped and enlarge which organ?
questions.explanation: Sickle cells can get stuck in the spleen, causing it to enlarge rapidly and leading to severe anaemia.

questions.question: Clinical stroke may affect what percentage of people with haemoglobin SS by age 45?
questions.explanation: As many as 24 percent of people with haemoglobin SS may suffer a clinical stroke by age 45.

questions.question: Which part of the eye is the most common site of damage in sickle cell disease?
questions.explanation: The retina is the most common site of eye damage, where blood vessels can overgrow, get blocked, or bleed.

questions.question: Males with sickle cell disease may experience painful, prolonged erections known as which condition?
questions.explanation: Priapism happens when blood flow out of the penis is blocked by sickled cells.

questions.question: Emergency medical care should be sought for priapism if the condition lasts for more than which duration?
questions.explanation: If priapism lasts for more than 4 hours, emergency medical care is required to avoid complications.

questions.question: When red cells haemolyse, haemoglobin breaks down into which substance that can form gallstones?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin breaks down into bilirubin, which can form stones that get stuck in the gallbladder.

questions.question: Doctors can diagnose SCD before a baby is born by testing which fluid?
questions.explanation: Prenatal screening involves using a sample of amniotic fluid to test for the sickle haemoglobin gene.

questions.question: Which medication is given twice a day to children with SCD to reduce the risk of severe pneumococcal infection?
questions.explanation: Taking penicillin two times a day has been shown to reduce severe infections caused by pneumococcus bacteria.

questions.question: At present, which medical procedure is considered the only cure for sickle cell disease?
questions.explanation: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is currently the only known cure for SCD.

questions.question: According to the trichromatic theory, the three types of cone cells react most strongly to which combination of lights?
questions.explanation: The three types of cones each have a pigment that reacts most strongly to red, green, and violet light.

questions.question: The highest concentration of cone cells in the eye is found in which structure?
questions.explanation: The highest concentration of cone cells is found in the macula, which is the central part of the retina.

questions.question: A severe liver complication in SCD where sickled cells block blood vessels in the liver is called what?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell intrahepatic cholestasis occurs when sickled cells block blood vessels in the liver.

questions.question: A Transcranial Doppler ultrasound screening is primarily used to check a child's risk for which complication?
questions.explanation: The Transcranial Doppler study can determine if a child is at higher risk for a stroke.

questions.question: Children with SCD often grow and develop more slowly than their peers primarily due to which condition?
questions.explanation: The text states that children with SCD may grow and develop more slowly because of anaemia.

questions.question: A joint complication in SCD caused by decreased oxygen flow to the bones is known as what?
questions.explanation: Decreased oxygen flow to bones in the hip, knees, and ankles can result in avascular or aseptic necrosis.

questions.question: Symptoms of acute chest syndrome in SCD may include chest pain along with which other sign?
questions.explanation: Symptoms of acute chest syndrome include chest pain, fever, shortness of breath, rapid breathing, and cough.

questions.question: People with SCD typically do not develop leg ulcers until they are past which age?
questions.explanation: The text notes that people with SCD usually do not get leg ulcers until after the age of 10.

questions.question: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is inherited in which genetic pattern?
questions.explanation: The condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern because the gene is located on the X chromosome.

questions.question: Carriers of a G6PD mutation are believed to have partial protection against which parasite?
questions.explanation: Carriers may be partially protected against Plasmodium, which causes malaria.

questions.question: Eating fava beans can trigger haemolytic anaemia in G6PD patients, producing a reaction known as which term?
questions.explanation: A reaction caused by eating fava beans or inhaling pollen from fava plants is called favism.

questions.question: Marfan syndrome is an inherited genetic disorder that follows which inheritance pattern?
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder where an affected parent has a 50% risk of passing it on.

questions.question: A defect in which specific glycoprotein is responsible for causing Marfan syndrome?
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome is caused by a defect in the FBN1 gene, which encodes the glycoprotein fibrillin-1.

questions.question: Dislocation of the eye lens in Marfan syndrome is medically known by which term?
questions.explanation: The medical term for lens dislocation caused by weak ciliary zonules is ectopia lentis.

questions.question: Identify the Marfan complication involving a tear in the innermost layer of the aortic wall.
questions.explanation: An aortic dissection occurs when a tear allows blood to squeeze between the layers of the aortic wall.

questions.question: Huntington's disease is caused by an expanded trinucleotide repeat of which sequence in the HTT gene?
questions.explanation: The disease results from expanded CAG triplet repeats, which produce an abnormal protein that damages brain cells.

questions.question: Involuntary jerking or writhing movements experienced by patients with Huntington's disease are called what?
questions.explanation: Chorea refers to the involuntary jerking or writhing movements seen in movement disorders associated with HD.

questions.question: Which symptom of Huntington's disease is primarily treated using the medication tetrabenazine?
questions.explanation: The best evidence for treating the movement problems associated with HD is with the medication tetrabenazine.
